name: Exact Prefix-Slope Formula
statement: For an order $\pi=(c_1,\ldots,c_m)$ and prefixes $C_j=\{c_1,\ldots,c_j\}$, $w(\pi)=\max_j g(C_j)=\max_j\nu_k(C_j)=\max_j\lambda_k(C_j)-1$. Minimizing any of these prefix maxima over all orders gives $\sigma(C)$; restricting to orders beginning with a prescribed nonempty subset $I$ gives $\sigma(C;I)$.
proof: A minimal predecessor disagreement at the addition of $c_j$ is exactly an empty-interval pair in $C_j$. The inequalities $g(C_j)\leq\nu_k(C_j)\leq\sigma(C_j)\leq w(\pi|_{C_j})\leq w(\pi)$ force the first two equalities. A prefix attaining a positive gap has a first syzygy of slope $w(\pi)+1$; the baseline slope handles width zero, while the general slope bound gives the reverse inequality.
